9: Fractional Head of AI vs full-time CAIO
10: What is a fractional Head of AI?
11: A fractional Head of AI is an experienced AI leader a company hires part-time instead of full-time. They take on the same accountability as a full-time Head of AI — priorities, governance, AI deployment and reporting to leadership — but only to the extent the company genuinely needs. It suits companies that need AI leadership but have neither the workload nor the budget for a full-time role.
12: How many days a month does a fractional Head of AI work?
13: The scope follows the company's needs and the phase of the engagement, not a fixed table. At the start, when the AI agenda is being kicked off, involvement tends to be more intense — typically on the order of one to two days a week. In the ongoing mode, a few days a month is enough to run the portfolio, the priorities and the reporting. The scope is agreed in advance and can be changed.
14: What is the difference between a fractional Head of AI and a consultant?
15: A consultant or an agency delivers a specific project or recommendation, but does not take on accountability for the whole AI agenda. A fractional Head of AI has the mandate to decide across the company, to hold the priorities, governance and budget, and to answer for the impact — just part-time. It is a leadership role, not a deliverable.
16: Does the fractional model pay off more than full-time?
17: For companies without a permanent full-time workload for this role — typically companies of 50 to 500 employees — usually yes. They get senior AI leadership without a year-round payroll cost, without several months of recruiting, and with a flexible commitment. A company with a permanent full-time need, by contrast, will move towards an internal Head of AI over time.
18: Does a fractional Head of AI ever move to a full-time role?
19: Yes, and that is the natural goal. When the AI agenda grows into a full-time role, the fractional Head of AI helps find an internal successor, onboard them and hand over a working system — the register, the rules, the agents and the metrics. The point is not to create permanent dependence, but to hand a managed agenda to an internal owner.

82: Who the fractional model is not for
83: Honestly — a fractional Head of AI is not a universal answer. It does not make sense in these situations:
84: Large companies with a permanent full-time workload.
85: When the AI agenda is big enough to occupy a person full-time along with a team, go straight for an internal Head of AI.
86: Companies where AI does not affect the business yet.
87: If it is side experiments, you do not need a leadership role — fractional or otherwise — yet.
88: Companies looking for a cheap implementer.
89: When you need one specific system built, you are looking for a supplier, not AI leadership.
